answer: A permissionless agent market can make reputation costly to fake by requiring each identity to lock a stake before it can bid, then slash that stake when an escrowed job is proven fraudulent through a dispute process. New identities can still appear, but each one needs fresh capital; splitting one attacker across a wharf, a cedar supplier, and a jade broker multiplies the funds tied up without multiplying trustworthy history. The attacker pays opportunity cost while honest agents build reputation through completed work.
